criteria.name: B4-1  Theorem 4: Bellman-Ford agrees with cycle enumeration
criteria.detail: 24 agree, 0 disagree over 24 graphs; 5 admit a sub-potential and 19 carry a positive cycle

criteria.name: B4-2  the returned potential satisfies every edge inequality
B4-3  Theorem 5: a sink component gives an unbounded ray
criteria.detail: 31 graphs with a proper sink; the worst violation over shifts up to 1e+06 is at machine precision for that scale, below 1e-09

criteria.name: B4-4  Theorem 5: strong connectivity bounds the polytope
criteria.detail: 24 strongly connected graphs; every proper subset breaks (smallest breach 1.000e+06); every coordinate interval is finite, non-empty and contains the returned potential, widest 2.055

criteria.name: B4-5  Theorem 6(1): the symmetric part is non-positive
B4-6  Theorem 6(3): the antisymmetric case reproduces Theorem 1 bitwise
criteria.detail: 12 fields, 0 mismatches; potentials compared as raw bytes after centring on the minimum

criteria.name: B4-7  section 5.1: the directed square splits into friction and index
criteria.detail: |S+S' - friction| and |S-S' - index| are both at machine precision, below `1e-10`, over 226 squares

criteria.name: B4-8  section 5.1: a common spread moves the friction and not the index
criteria.detail: index unchanged to machine precision, below `1e-10`; friction moved by at least 2.223e-01

criteria.name: B4-9  Theorem 6(4): the index part is bounded by the friction part
criteria.detail: `S <= 0 and S' <= 0` and `|S-S'| <= -(S+S')` agree on all 226 squares, 52 of which have both cycles non-positive; the bound is what Theorem 4 buys once it is applied to each cycle rather than to their sum
